edits.old: Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary and are copied from RWB-E1-008. The harness owns no schema, no table and no field: it reads through the two decision read endpoints and calls the services' own write paths for every append it needs.
edits.new: Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary and are copied from RWB-E1-008. The harness owns no schema, no table and no field: it reads through the two decision read endpoints and calls the services' own write paths for every append it needs. Each wave-1 service holds its local record in the table decision_record, created through the decision-record library in its own schema; the DDL is set in the DB story of each service, and the case reference and the trace ID travel in inputsRef. The strict-mode confirmation is the read GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log/{entryId}, which returns 200 once the entry is sealed, together with the sealed-entry announcement on rwb.decision-record.v1 for the reporting projection. The ledger has no REST append operation: rwb_decision.decision_log_entry is written only by the ingest of rwb.decision-record.v1. decision_log_entry.case_id is a plain uuid with no foreign key, and the case is verified over the P3 case contract.

edits.old: Those are record references and codes, never a business value invented by this story.
edits.new: Those are record references and codes, never a business value invented by this story. Ingest into the central ledger dedupes on the CloudEvents id, orders per case from the producer, and rwb-decision assigns chain_seq and prev_hash under the chain lock, with catch-up within five minutes.
